articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Surrender
articles.dek: The Chemical Brothers released Surrender on 21 June 1999, on their own Freestyle Dust. A club duo who could not sing hired people who could, one track at a time.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Walking Wounded
articles.dek: Virgin released Everything but the Girl’s Walking Wounded in Europe on 6 May 1996. Todd Terry’s remix of Missing had already turned the duo into a dancefloor fact. This is the album that took the fact seriously.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Play
articles.dek: Mute released Moby’s Play on 17 May 1999. It set Alan Lomax’s field singers inside electronic songs, then licensed every track. The singers were not the ones who got paid.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Get Ready!
articles.dek: Get Ready for This began as a white-label instrumental in Antwerp in May 1991. The voices, the British edit, and the sports arenas came after.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Silent Shout
articles.dek: The Knife released Silent Shout on their own Rabid Records in Sweden on 17 February 2006. Britain got it on 20 March through Brille. Karin Dreijer’s voice is pitched until it becomes a character.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Ray of Light
articles.dek: Ray of Light, February 1998, is a William Orbit record. Madonna hired the Guerilla and Strange Cargo producer and refused to sand his machines down.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Deliverance
articles.dek: Baby D’s only album, Deliverance, came out on Systematic on 8 February 1996. The number one that paid for it, Let Me Be Your Fantasy, was already two years old.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Homework
articles.dek: Daft Punk’s debut left a Paris flat in January 1997. The 12-inch that mattered, Da Funk, had been out on Soma since May 1995.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Snivilisation
articles.dek: FFRR released Orbital’s Snivilisation in August 1994. Alison Goldfrapp’s first released vocal is on it, on Are We Here?

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Funcrusher Plus
articles.dek: Company Flow’s debut came out on Rawkus on 22 July 1997. El-P, Bigg Jus and Mr. Len had already put the Funcrusher EP out themselves in 1995.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Music for the Jilted Generation
articles.dek: XL released The Prodigy’s Music for the Jilted Generation on 4 July 1994. It went to number one in Britain. Their Law named the Criminal Justice Bill in the middle of a rave album.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Criminology
articles.dek: Raekwon and Ghostface Killah put Criminology out on 26 June 1995, ahead of Only Built 4 Cuban Linx…, which Loud and RCA released on 1 August.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Fat of the Land
articles.dek: XL released The Prodigy’s The Fat of the Land on 30 June 1997. It went to number one in Britain and America. Then Liam Howlett tried to blow the popularity up with one title.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: New Forms
articles.dek: Talkin’ Loud released Roni Size / Reprazent’s New Forms on 23 June 1997. It reached number 8 in Britain, stayed on the chart for 46 weeks, and won the Mercury Prize.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Inferno
articles.dek: Warp released Boards of Canada’s Inferno on 29 May 2026, catalogue WARP496. It is their first studio album since Tomorrow’s Harvest in 2013. The vinyl credits most of the writing to Mike Sandison.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Cold Vein
articles.dek: Definitive Jux released Cannibal Ox’s The Cold Vein on 15 May 2001. It was the label’s first full-length. El-P produced all of it. Vast Aire and Vordul Mega wrote it.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Infamous
articles.dek: Loud, RCA and BMG released Mobb Deep’s The Infamous on 25 April 1995. Juvenile Hell, in 1993, had not settled it. Shook Ones, Pt. II had been out since 7 February.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Music Has the Right to Children
articles.dek: Warp and Skam released Boards of Canada’s Music Has the Right to Children on 20 April 1998. Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin recorded it at Hexagon Sun. Twoism and Hi Scores had already circulated in small runs.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Illmatic
articles.dek: Nas’s debut, Columbia, 19 April 1994, was built by Premier, Large Professor, Pete Rock, Q-Tip and L.E.S. The shipments took years to catch the reputation.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Blue Lines
articles.dek: Massive Attack’s debut came out on 8 April 1991, on Wild Bunch and Virgin. The singles had already been in public for months. The slow tempo was the decision.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Frankie Knuckles
articles.dek: Frankie Knuckles died in Chicago on 31 March 2014, aged 59. He had been the resident at the Warehouse. Your Love, with Jamie Principle, is the record to carry.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Black Secret Technology
articles.dek: Gerald Simpson put Black Secret Technology out on his own Juice Box label in March 1995, after 28 Gun Bad Boy and after Voodoo Ray, and he let the singers stay in the track.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
articles.dek: Warp released Aphex Twin’s Selected Ambient Works Volume II on 7 March 1994. Most of the pieces have no titles. Sire released it on 12 April.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Madvillainy
articles.dek: Stones Throw released Madvillainy, MF DOOM and Madlib, on 23 March 2004. The songs are short. The mask and the loop get equal time.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Maxinquaye
articles.dek: Tricky released Maxinquaye on 20 February 1995. Martina Topley-Bird sang it. The title is his mother’s name, Maxine Quaye.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Dubnobasswithmyheadman
articles.dek: Junior Boy’s Own released dubnobasswithmyheadman on 24 January 1994. It was the label’s first album, and the first Underworld record with Darren Emerson in the group.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Jack Your Body
articles.dek: Steve “Silk” Hurley’s Jack Your Body spent two weeks at number one in Britain in January 1987. It was the first house record to do that.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Leftism
articles.dek: Leftfield released Leftism on 30 January 1995, on their own Hard Hands label and on Columbia. Open Up, with John Lydon, had already been a single in 1993.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Strait Is Not a Scene
articles.dek: Club Copy’s Bandcamp names Cumberland. The roster reaches Athens. A catalogue with a return address is not a scene.
articles.imageAlt: Champion Sound — L.T. Drifta, camouflage disc

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: NIGHTSHIFT, Vol. 3
articles.dek: NIGHTSHIFT Vol. 3 runs 1:19:57 on L.T. Drifta’s SoundCloud, posted 2 October 2026 UTC. No public tracklist.
articles.imageAlt: VCR Recordings label art — Summer Madness

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Romford Kept the Receipts
articles.dek: Mega Mega opens in a soon-to-close South Street club, and it brings Boogie Times, Suburban Base and a decade of Essex white labels back under one roof.
articles.imageAlt: A lone pair of black loudspeakers on a tripod stand against a pale wall, no one around.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Still Looking for the Warehouse
articles.dek: In Pursuit of Repetitive Beats puts a visitor in a car, a service station, and a 1989 acid-house chase at Sensoria in Sheffield.
articles.imageAlt: An empty warehouse with concrete pillars, corrugated metal walls and a scuffed bare floor under strip lights.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Radial Wants the Midsize Room
articles.dek: Tottenham’s new 250-cap listening club opens out of Ten87 Studios with a Whitaker-tuned Martin Audio/Funktion-One rig, a no-phones floor, and an opening weekend that stacks jungle, UK bass, house and garage. The gossip is the sound. The story is the room.
articles.imageAlt: Empty disco floor, mirrored ball overhead, speakers in the dark, no people. Photo: Yerutskow, CC BY-SA 3.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: They Settled It at Afterhours
articles.dek: Madonna clapped back at Charli xcx’s dead-dancefloor line. Then they wrote the afters together.
articles.imageAlt: Empty neon corridor in pink and blue light, no people. Render: Wizarto Pro, Unsplash License.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Eight Rooms, One Basement
articles.dek: From 2008 to 2012 the Guvernment was eighth in the world. Toronto’s other night was a basement under the Silver Dollar, and a tent in a park.
articles.imageAlt: The Hotel Waverly at 484 Spadina in daylight, white brick, the Silver Dollar awning and round sign at street level.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Thirty Years on the Calendar
articles.dek: ADE’s 30th runs 21–25 October: more than 3,600 artists, 1,300 events and 300 rooms, plus a panel asking why anyone needs a dancefloor.
articles.imageAlt: The round silver gas holder at Westergasfabriek in daylight, brick arches along the base, two pointed brick porches, an empty paved yard

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Across the Street
articles.dek: Melkweg soft-opened Club Annie in the old Sugarfactory. The pilot is two years, the ADE weekender is thirty hours, and the phone rule is a test.
articles.imageAlt: Melkweg at night, green neon on the brick gable, a glass hall to the left, canal houses and bicycles along the water

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Deep Sleep
articles.dek: On 15 October 2026 Roni Size played a timber booth 1,375 feet under a Welsh slate mine. The world-record claim went out as a submission.
articles.imageAlt: A timber DJ booth with a corrugated roof inside a slate cavern, teal climbing helmets in the crowd, hands raised, G-SHOCK Sessions projected on the rock

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: No Undo
articles.dek: On 7 October 2026 Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety he plans to stop making synthesizers, OP-1 included. DJ Mag wrote it up on 15 October.
articles.imageAlt: A white Teenage Engineering OP-1 under blue light, tape reels on the screen, colored knobs above the keys

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Doors at Six
articles.dek: Pokémon Night Out calls itself a party. At The O2 it is Tuesday 10 November, doors at 6, with Marshmello and Alison Wonderland. The stream stays in Los Angeles.
articles.imageAlt: Pikachu mascots in a Yokohama street parade, yellow costumes with black-tipped ears, one wearing a flower crown

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: While He Was Playing
articles.dek: At PRST in Vienna, someone took Demuja’s USB out of the CDJ mid-set. The room went quiet. The unreleased music left with the crowd.
articles.imageAlt: Flyer for PRST on 8 October 2026, Demuja billed from 22:00 with Namimi Sensei, Satoshi DJ Yoshida and Gen, and DJ Yotsuya

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: All Night, One Name
articles.dek: Ibiza’s closing week gave Manda Moor, Mau P and Sirus Hood a room until morning. Everywhere else the poster split into pairs.
articles.imageAlt: The Pacha cherries lit pink behind horizontal slats in a round window

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Missing P
articles.dek: Sebadoh's Harmacy turns thirty on November 20 with sixteen extra tracks and a zine drawn by Lou Barlow, who has called the record a heartbreaker. A band that began on home-made cassettes got a Sub Pop budget, a studio and, by Barlow's account, a drummer problem. What is an album worth to the person who made it?
articles.imageAlt: Sebadoh performing, a guitarist at a microphone under red stage light.
articles.credit: Photo: parttimemusic, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Six Times
articles.dek: DJ Mag crowned David Guetta No. 1 for a sixth time. The top two names held. Under them, three DJs climbed 22 places and split one prize.
articles.imageAlt: David Guetta and MORTEN behind Pioneer decks at Hï Ibiza in 2022, blue stage light, MORTEN with both arms up

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Signals From the Heart of the Rave
articles.dek: Rupture turns twenty with a book written by the people on its floor, and a love letter to the South London arches it called home for eighteen years.
articles.imageAlt: Dark brick arch tunnel, warm light at the far end, no people. Photo: Badr Outal, CC BY 3.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Last Issue
articles.dek: The Skinny spent two decades writing down Scotland's nights out. Now it is gone, and one zine has to ask another's question: who keeps the record?
articles.imageAlt: Stack of blank paper pages, no titles, no people. Photo: Kasia Sikorska, Pexels License.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Drake Went Hot Topic and the Internet Lost Its Mind
articles.dek: Pinkchyu walked him into the mall, spiked the choker, and set Princess to a private Medieval Times. Rollout genius or midlife meme. The timeline cannot pick one.
articles.imageAlt: Pinkchyu in black, studded choker and dark lip, mall light behind her

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Crystal Tears on the Westside
articles.dek: Six years after Chilombo, Jhené Aiko finishes Westside Whimsy the way she started: mixtape stubbornness, Fisticuffs in the booth, and a love letter to a coast that burned.
articles.imageAlt: Jhené Aiko close-up on teal, crystal gems falling like tears under both eyes : Westside Whimsy album cover

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: No Fun City Still Raids the Rooms
articles.dek: Vancouver sells vibrant nightlife to the visitor brochure, then inspects the rooms that actually dance.
articles.imageAlt: Vancouver skyline at night from Spanish Banks, towers across the water.
articles.credit: Photo: Jerry Meaden, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Madame Lou's Is Dead. Bottlerocket Wants the Basement.
articles.dek: Two Crocodile rooms gone, a hundred jobs cut, a comedy sale, and a March 2027 target for the basement.
articles.imageAlt: The Crocodile Cafe on Second Avenue in Belltown, Seattle, seen from the street.
articles.credit: Photo: Joe Mabel, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Portland Finally Got an All-Ages Temple
articles.dek: The Dancin' Bare is a Friends of Noise room now: no liquor, four hundred caps, and the bloodline showed up with a drum kit.
articles.imageAlt: Downtown Portland, Oregon at night, street lights and mid-rise blocks.
articles.credit: Photo: Tony Webster, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Party Like the Lease Is Ending
articles.dek: Cobalt came back as punk, metal, hardcore, then a dance floor till two, with a hotel clock in the coverage and a fire that was only a blip.
articles.imageAlt: The Cobalt Motor Hotel at 917 Main Street, Vancouver, in daylight.
articles.credit: Photo: Gates of Ale, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: FIFA vs the Underground
articles.dek: Granville posted a record week and the warehouses posted shutdowns. Two nightlives, same city, same winter.
articles.imageAlt: BC Place stadium in Vancouver, the roof and the plaza in daylight.
articles.credit: Photo: Mike, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: They Licensed the Remix Back to You
articles.dek: UMG hands ElevenLabs the mash-up keys the same week Suno drops “industry partner” v6, while Universal is still suing somebody.
articles.imageAlt: A DJ mixer on a table, faders and knobs, no one at it.
articles.credit: Photo: Jana C., public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Mouse Hired an Empire
articles.dek: deadmau5 leaves CAA for IAG — the flex isn’t the festival slot, it’s the software, the series, the IP stack.
articles.imageAlt: deadmau5 performing live, mask on, one leg raised.
articles.credit: Photo: GoatLordServant, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Just Sports Means Equity
articles.dek: Sydney Sweeney didn’t endorse Novig. She joined the cap table, and celebrity A&R grew up.
articles.imageAlt: Sydney Sweeney at a premiere, photographed by Glenn Francis.
articles.credit: Photo: Glenn Francis, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Stars for the Floor
articles.dek: This week’s reading.
articles.imageAlt: A 1976 Eisenhower dollar, moon reverse. Photo: AKS.9955, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Shoes Come Off
articles.dek: Afters begin in the hallway, where boots and wet socks become the real door policy. Leave them by the entrance, or you’re still at the club.
articles.imageAlt: Black 1990s platform pumps on a patterned rug.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Mini Held Nothing
articles.dek: The bag is the size of a tin on purpose (lip, key, phone in the boot), and it was never meant to carry anyone else’s night.
articles.imageAlt: Tiny studded black clutch with silver chain.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Mezzanine
articles.dek: Circa and Virgin released Massive Attack’s Mezzanine on 20 April 1998. It entered the UK albums chart at number one on 2 May. Andrew Vowles left in the aftermath.
articles.imageAlt: Disco balls hanging in the dark.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Sticker on the Lens
articles.dek: They banned phones at the door in the name of presence, then posted the night before the taxi did, and the no-phone rule became another flyer.
articles.imageAlt: Four disposable film cameras with flash.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Bathroom Line
articles.dek: The floor is for the photograph, but the stall is where the night gets finished, the lip redrawn and the decision made while somebody holds the door with a boot.
articles.imageAlt: Cookies nightclub restroom, Berlin. Photo: Siegfy, CC BY-SA 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Are We Still Going
articles.dek: Resident Advisor lists the night and Dice sells the ticket. The address still moves the way it moved in 1998: person to person.
articles.imageAlt: A phone on a table. Photo: Santeri Viinamäki, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Flyer on the Fridge
articles.dek: The flyer was the first pressing of the night: cheap paper, a date, and a record of a room that did not issue one.
articles.imageAlt: A 1992 Ultim-8 rave flyer. Photo: ultim8 raves, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Incense Before the Aux
articles.dek: Before anyone touches the speaker, somebody lights a stick. The afters live or die on whether the apartment already smelled like a night.
articles.imageAlt: Smoke from an incense stick. Photo: AntanO, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Pants Stay On
articles.dek: Nine signatures on a 6 February 2026 petition tried to police pajama pants. The flyers were already printing the cat.
articles.imageAlt: Pink pajama pants on a warehouse dancefloor, flash photo.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: You Are (Love)
articles.dek: Riscape's CC004: four house tracks, 15:02, released 18 September 2026. Bandcamp titles the last one Days Like This.
articles.imageAlt: You Are (Love) circular dusk cityscape artwork

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Riscape: Heads Down
articles.dek: John Rigas trained as a pianist in Chalandri, released house on a Dutch label, and has two Club Copy EPs under the name Riscape.
articles.imageAlt: Riscape

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: She Showed Up
articles.dek: On 25 May 2025 Lorde stood in the crowd at Mary's Underground in Sydney for a night of her own song.
articles.imageAlt: A concert crowd facing the stage. Photo: Alpharockindia, CC BY-SA 3.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Fancy That
articles.dek: PinkPantheress, nine tracks and twenty minutes, no features, and she still doesn’t want a long outro.
articles.imageAlt: A TDK cassette, overhead. Photo: Scott Schiller, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Eusexua
articles.dek: Twigs made a word for the second before you come back into your body, and album three is out today.
articles.imageAlt: People on a dancefloor. Photo: CC0 / Wikimedia Commons.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: She's Never Been to Berghain
articles.dek: Rosalía, Björk, Yves Tumor, the LSO, German in the first breath, and then she said she’s never been inside.
articles.imageAlt: Graffiti steel doors, Berlin. Photo by Michael Mayer, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Labubu on the Strap
articles.dek: Lisa clipped a gremlin to a Louis, Dua doubled up, and reseller tabs went ugly. The floor still cared more about the boots than the StockX screenshot.
articles.imageAlt: A clear plastic teddy charm. Photo by Michael Scialdone, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Headphones On
articles.dek: Addison’s debut is twelve tracks and no features. Charli said trust the ideas, and I did on the walk home.
articles.imageAlt: A Sony Walkman WM-FX151. Photo: YoloBoscaiolo, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: MAYHEM
articles.dek: Fourteen tracks, Gesaffelstein on Killah, and Abracadabra never left the kitchen after the Grammys.
articles.imageAlt: An empty arena from above, stage lights still on. Photo: Richard West, CC BY-SA 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Boiler Room Got Sold
articles.dek: On 15 January 2025 DICE sold Boiler Room to Superstruct. The stream had a landlord. The night never had.
articles.imageAlt: A security camera on a wall. Photo: CC BY-SA 3.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: You Have to Flip It
articles.dek: Luminate’s 2026 midyear report counted US physical album sales up 7.8 percent, to 38.2 million. CDs rose faster than vinyl. The RIAA’s dollar figure for physical revenue rose 25.9 percent. Units and money are two different counts.
articles.imageAlt: A Fuji compact cassette on a ledge. You have to flip it. Photo: R. Henrik Nilsson, CC BY 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Nobody Asked What to Put On
articles.dek: The photograph shows the peak. The rest of the night starts when someone plays a record and nobody votes on it.
articles.imageAlt: A record spinning on a home player.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Istanbul Pulled the Lights
articles.dek: Istanbul pulled Anyma after comments called the lights satanic. Tickets were still for sale.
articles.imageAlt: An empty arena from above, stage lights still on. Photo: Richard West, CC BY-SA 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Love Deluxe
articles.dek: Sade's fourth album, Epic, 26 October 1992. Quiet, on this record, is a decision with a rhythm section under it.
articles.imageAlt: Sade Love Deluxe album cover. The record you put on when people are still in the apartment.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: They Put the Verse in Court
articles.dek: In September 2026 the Met defended drill lyrics as evidence. A report counted 252 defendants in three years.
articles.imageAlt: A wooden gavel on a courtroom bench. Photo by Joe Gratz, CC0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: You Bought a Place in Line
articles.dek: In the 2026 DJ Mag poll Berghain placed 21st. A ticket buys a place in line. The door can still refund you.
articles.imageAlt: Graffiti steel doors, Berlin. Photo by Michael Mayer, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Velvet Rope
articles.dek: Virgin released Janet Jackson’s The Velvet Rope on 7 October 1997. Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis produced it. She described the rope as the line around who gets let in.
articles.imageAlt: Gold stanchions with thick red ropes.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: I’m Outside
articles.dek: They’re already on the curb in the rain. The blue bubble says I’m outside. Your other boot is still missing, and the night is starting without you.
articles.imageAlt: Red neon NIGHT CLUB sign on a city street at night.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Jersey Stayed On
articles.dek: A football shirt under the strobe isn’t matchday cosplay. It’s the same comfort argument as the pajama pants, only with better colour and a badge as jewelry.
articles.imageAlt: Football jersey worn as street fashion with jeans and Jordans.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: They Sold the Afters
articles.dek: Dice listed an afters for twenty-five at the door of a kitchen, and the pin that used to be the ticket got replaced by a checkout button.
articles.imageAlt: Friends in a warm kitchen late at night, wine glasses on the counter.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Last Emperor
articles.dek: Sakamoto, Byrne, and Cong Su scored The Last Emperor in 1987. The music holds up with the film turned off.
articles.imageAlt: The Last Emperor soundtrack cover. child emperor and bowing figure under a yellow banner

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: We Signed Forsberg
articles.dek: Forsberg’s Bandcamp bio is one line, house from Cumberland, and the music page now holds ten titles.
articles.imageAlt: Forsberg

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Revibed Isn't Digging
articles.dek: Revibed has sold digital rips of rare records since 2024 and called it caretaking. Terre Thaemlitz told them to stop. Resident Advisor reported the charge on 22 December 2025.
articles.imageAlt: Worn artist tabs in a record shop.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Born I Sat Down
articles.dek: Born I, a DC producer, toured Hip Hop Soundbaths with Plum Village monastics. The album is called AMIDA.
articles.imageAlt: Incense sticks in a temple bucket. Photo: Angelo Marcellano, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: any jungle
articles.dek: The 30 August 2026 note reviewed a L.T. Drifta title the artist page's seven-record list does not include.
articles.imageAlt: White vinyl on black with melting Club Copy lettering. any jungle

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: j'adore
articles.dek: Two Forsberg tracks, 10 August 2026. Bandcamp times them 3:27 and 4:51. The sleeve credits CJ Archer as producer.
articles.imageAlt: Fisheye photo of a blue car at dusk. j'adore

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Champion Sound
articles.dek: CC001 is one instrumental track, 4:53, dated 9 July 2024 on Bandcamp. The catalogue number and the public date agree.
articles.imageAlt: Champion Sound circular logo artwork

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Lions’ Gate
articles.dek: A 1 June 2024 note named a L.T. Drifta cut after the bridge. The current artist page does not list the title.
articles.imageAlt: Vancouver street at night. Rooms sign, alley wires

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Dummy
articles.dek: Portishead's debut, Go! Beat, 22 August 1994: a Bristol album that made the sample feel like a voice.
articles.imageAlt: Rain on a window. Photo: W.carter, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: Club Copy
articles.headline: Buried Treasure
articles.dek: Digging is a method. The find is the record you almost put back. Most afternoons you leave with wet shoes and nothing.
articles.imageAlt: Record bins in a shop. Flip until something holds.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Part No Prompt Can Touch
articles.dek: A model can imitate a finished track. It cannot supply the months a person disappeared into before the bridge existed.
articles.imageAlt: A computer lab. Photo: Tariqabjotu, CC BY-SA 3.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Summer Madness
articles.dek: Eight short electronic tracks, released 14 November 2025. The Bandcamp sleeve times Summer Madness at 20:35.
articles.imageAlt: Hands framing a sunset over misty hills. Summer Madness

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: L.T. Drifta on Club Copy
articles.dek: Six titles on L.T. Drifta’s Bandcamp, from a standards album in 2025 to Renegade Snares on 23 October, plus the mixes on SoundCloud.
articles.imageAlt: L.T. Drifta

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Endtroducing
articles.dek: DJ Shadow's 1996 Mo' Wax debut: an album built from other people's records, and a method with a pulse.
articles.imageAlt: DJ Shadow Endtroducing album cover. crate diggers in a record shop

articles.author: Club Copy
articles.headline: Beat Tape
articles.dek: A 22 August 2023 note announced a CJ Archer beat tape. The current Club Copy catalogue does not list one.
articles.imageAlt: Club Copy oval logo with star on textured gray

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: It Goes Like Nanana
articles.dek: Peggy Gou’s Nanana as the aux between the kitchen and the gorge — Italo sunshine from a booth that already put in the hours.
articles.imageAlt: A rave crowd, 2008. Photo: Ildar Sagdejev, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Initial D and the Sound of Speed
articles.dek: Initial D paired a mountain pass with eurobeat. The soundtrack outlived the joke and taught a tempo what devotion sounds like.
articles.imageAlt: A winding mountain road. Photo: jazpillaga, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Ahmad Jamal '73
articles.dek: Ahmad Jamal '73, on 20th Century Records: the trio's sense of space, moved onto electric piano.
articles.imageAlt: Ahmad Jamal '73 album cover. pop-art portrait with hand on cheek

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Desert Played the Sad Banger
articles.dek: Four Tet, Fred again.., and Skrillex under one Coachella sunset — Cumberland watched from the kitchen like it was a voice note.
articles.imageAlt: Desert at dusk. Photo: Kerry Bolger, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Donuts
articles.dek: J Dilla's Donuts, Stones Throw, 7 February 2006: thirty-one short instrumentals, released three days before he died.
articles.imageAlt: J Dilla Donuts album cover. smiling portrait in a Detroit D cap

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Floor Already Knew
articles.dek: Honey Dijon's Black Girl Magic, on Classic Music Company: a house album that casts guests without becoming a compilation.
articles.imageAlt: A disco ball. Photo: CC BY-SA 3.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Easy on Your Own
articles.dek: Alvvays came back with Blue Rev, named for a Canadian cooler and built for the night drive that doesn’t end.
articles.imageAlt: A highway at night. Photo: Rick Doble, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Come for Me
articles.dek: Shygirl’s Nymph is thirty-two minutes of club bathroom light — Nike, Shlut, and a body that doesn’t ask permission.
articles.imageAlt: A bathroom sink. Photo: Chris McKenna, public domain.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Baddest of Them All
articles.dek: Eliza Rose and Interplanetary Criminal's B.O.T.A.: a UK garage chant that reached the Top 10 with Lisa Lisa in the sample.
articles.imageAlt: A DJ booth in Munich. Photo: Arnold Jaeger Werner, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: What I Want
articles.dek: MUNA’s chorus doesn’t whisper — silk chiffon, a gay bar, and a kitchen disco bulb with everybody’s ex in the other room.
articles.imageAlt: A disco ball on a ceiling. Photo: Phillip Pessar, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: American Teenager
articles.dek: Ethel Cain’s Preacher’s Daughter is the highway record — church, motels, and a girl who kept the aux like a weapon.
articles.imageAlt: Supai Motel neon at night. Photo: G. Edward Johnson, CC BY 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Bike, Not the Ballad
articles.dek: Rosalía’s MOTOMAMI refuses the wedding-slideshow ballad — SAOKO, CHICKEN TERIYAKI, tradition you ride instead of frame.
articles.imageAlt: A motorcycle. Photo: Daniel K. Gebhart, CC BY 2.5.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: She Called It the Summer of Jungle
articles.dek: Nia Archives' Forbidden Feelingz, on her label HIJINXX: Bradford, jungle tempo, and a title that names Maya Angelou.
articles.imageAlt: A forest path. Public domain.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Working for the Knife
articles.dek: Mitski’s Laurel Hell as fluorescent shift energy — the knife and the thing it cuts, then a Cumberland walk to the car in February.
articles.imageAlt: A kitchen sink. Photo: Larry McElhiney, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Mixtape Didn't Ask
articles.dek: FKA twigs put the club on a mixtape, and the kitchen already had the aux.
articles.imageAlt: A gas station at night. Photo: Doug Davey, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: Club Copy
articles.headline: CJ Archer
articles.dek: The 27 October 2022 conversation, kept as printed, and read against the catalogue the label actually released.
articles.imageAlt: A computer desk. Photo: Dhivyabsk, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: To Hell With It
articles.dek: PinkPantheress, To Hell With It, October 2021: short songs, garage drums, a bedroom upload that became the record.
articles.imageAlt: A home recording setup. Photo: Subhashish Panigrahi, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Rooms Opened
articles.dek: On 19 July 2021 England let the nightclubs open again. Fabric had about 900 people in. A vaccine pass was not required. A lateral-flow test got you a shorter queue.
articles.imageAlt: De School dancefloor, Amsterdam. Photo: Martijn Savenije, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Oil and Chrome
articles.dek: SOPHIE died in Athens on 30 January 2021. The records, from BIPP to OIL OF EVERY PEARL'S UN-INSIDES, were already finished.
articles.imageAlt: Oil on wet asphalt. Photo: Aniskov, CC BY 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Essential Listening: Untrue
articles.dek: Burial's second album, Hyperdub, 5 November 2007: garage slowed down until the walk home is the song.
articles.imageAlt: Rain on a window. Photo: W.carter, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Kitchen Was the Club
articles.dek: In April 2021 there was no door and no cloakroom, just a link, a stick of incense, and socks on linoleum while someone DJed from another province.
articles.imageAlt: An apartment kitchen. Photo: Gogerr, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Coat on the Chair
articles.dek: In June 2021 the going-out top stayed on and the coat never left the kitchen chair. There was no cloakroom to prove you’d meant to leave, only the fit as evidence.
articles.imageAlt: A wet Vancouver street at dusk. The coat walked out with nowhere to check it.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The File Is the Record
articles.dek: Bandcamp started waiving its revenue share on Bandcamp Fridays in March 2020. By April 2024 the company said fans had paid more than $120 million to artists and labels on those days. The download was the copy you could play while the plant slipped.
articles.imageAlt: A Fuji compact cassette on a ledge. Photo: R. Henrik Nilsson, CC BY 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Wristband in the Drawer
articles.dek: You kept the first night back in cheap plastic you don’t wear. It isn’t a shrine, just proof that a door existed again after the rooms wobbled.
articles.imageAlt: A Vancouver festival wristband. Photo: Richard Eriksson, CC BY 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Platforms Came Back
articles.dek: When the rooms opened for real in April 2022, everyone who got dressed arrived in Buffalo height they’d practiced on linoleum, a heel that remembered 1999 before the trend reports did.
articles.imageAlt: Platform heels. Photo: Stevelefrancais, CC BY-SA 4.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: Homogenic
articles.dek: Björk's third album, 1997, with Mark Bell and a string octet: beats and orchestra in the same bar.
articles.imageAlt: Mountains reflected in a pond, Iceland. Photo: Eric Kilby, CC BY-SA 2.0.

articles.author: CJ Archer
articles.headline: The Algorithm Is Not a Room
articles.dek: Eliza Rose and Interplanetary Criminal’s B.O.T.A. was released on 15 June 2022, entered the UK chart on 4 August, and reached number one on 2 September. The year-end graphic came afterwards.
articles.imageAlt: A security camera on a wall. Photo: CC BY-SA 3.0.
